nodes.question: What steps were involved in the literature search strategy described in the methodology?
nodes.answer: The steps included identifying databases and search terms, screening articles, categorizing selected articles, and synthesizing and analyzing the articles.
nodes.paragraph: There is no one-size-fits-all solution to mitigate the envi- ronmental burden of EHDs. Solutions such as eco-design strategies, replacing single-use with reusable EHDs, circu- lar economy strategies, and proper treatment and disposal could enhance the overall sustainability of the healthcare industry. However, the perceived environmental benefits of these strategies are not yet fully understood, nor is the effect on environmental sustainability when considering direct and indirect impacts. To address the above-mentioned shortcom- ings, this study focuses on two objectives: (1) to investi- gate the current state of knowledge on the evaluation of the environmental sustainability of EHDs and (2) to identify research gaps in environmental impact evaluation studies and make recommendations using LCA perspective as the backbone. 2 Methodology This section starts with a brief description of the search strategy used to identify and select eligible studies on the environmental sustainability assessment of EHDs. Subse- quently, the method for extracting data and analysing infor - mation from the selected studies is described. 2.1 Literature search strategy The literature search followed a structured procedure involv - ing the following steps: (i) identifying the databases and search terms, (ii) screening articles, (iii) categorising the selected articles, and (iv) synthesising and analysing the articles.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many studies were identified from the three search engines?
nodes.answer: A total of 2696 studies were identified from the three search engines.
nodes.paragraph: The literature studies were sought from three research engines: PubMED, Scopus, and Embase. The search phrases were built as a combination of keywords associated with EHDs and environmental assessment. The search was divided into two categories of search phrases. 640 The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment (2025) 30:638 653 In the first category, the search phrases were created as a combination of electronic healthcare device and keywords related to environmental assessment. In the second category, search phrases were built as a combination of digital health device and the same keywords from category one. This procedure is presented in Fig. 1. The temporal scope of the search was limited to articles published between 2013 and April 2023. Also, only English-language, peer-reviewed arti- cles were selected for screening. A total of 2696 studies were identified from the three search engines. 2.2 Screening criteria The yielded studies from the search engines were screened using a two-step process: title and abstract screening and full article screening. The former was performed to identify articles that fit the scope of the research, while studies that fell outside the healthcare sector S scope were excluded.
